mechanism_inventory: missing invariant enforcement (maxSupply check uses pre-mint totalSupply, not post-mint)
external-call failure / DoS (onZetaMessage/onZetaRevert callback can revert, blocking TSS delivery)
hook caller/timing mismatch (tokens minted before callback — CEI violation enabling reentrancy)
access-control mismatch (onReceive lacks whenNotPaused, unlike send and onRevert)
victim accounting direction (replay/double-mint via duplicate internalSendHash — no replay guard visible)
value exceeds bound (maxSupply default 2^256-1 effectively disables cap)

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: onReceive is not guarded by whenNotPaused, while send and onRevert are. When paused, TSS can still mint via onReceive, defeating the pause invariant — supply inflation or delivery to addresses that should be frozen during incident response.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Requires TSS key (privileged). Impact is protocol-invariant violation: pause is incomplete; onReceive keeps minting during an emergency halt.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Admin pause() (paused=true). 2. TSS calls onReceive(destinationAddress, zetaValue) — no whenNotPaused. 3. Tokens minted despite pause. 4. If message.length>0, callback executes too.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Protocol/users — pause invariant violated; minting continues during emergency halt.
selected_mechanisms.who_gains: destinationAddress receives minted tokens despite pause; compromised TSS enables inflation during believed-paused window.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Access-control asymmetry between sibling functions (different lifecycle state, paused); core cross-chain authz invariant.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: CEI violation in onReceive/onRevert: tokens minted before the external callback. Although gated by onlyTssAddress (direct re-entry into onReceive blocked), the callback CAN call send() (permissionless) to burn the just-minted tokens and emit a new ZetaSent — phantom cross-chain transaction TSS may honor on destination chain, doubling cross-chain value flow.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Conditional: requires control of destinationAddress (any user deploys a receiver) and that TSS routes a message there.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. Deploy malicious ZetaReceiver X. 2. Cross-chain send targets X with a message. 3. TSS onReceive mints to X. 4. X.onZetaMessage calls send() burning tokens, emitting phantom ZetaSent. 5. TSS may honor on destination, doubling value.
selected_mechanisms.who_loses: Destination chain token supply / cross-chain accounting integrity.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Different state (cross-chain accounting/totalSupply) and actor (permissionless receiver) than pause; send()-inside-callback not blocked by onlyTssAddress.

selected_mechanisms.root_cause: No replay protection on internalSendHash in connector source; onReceive/onRevert accept arbitrary internalSendHash with no on-chain mapping. If TSS re-submits same hash, mint() called again.
selected_mechanisms.attacker_model: Depends on whether mint() enforces uniqueness on internalSendHash (not in source). If not, duplicate submission double-mints.
selected_mechanisms.exploit_path: 1. onReceive(H, V) mints. 2. onReceive(H, V) again. 3. No connector check; mint again; supply inflated by V.
selected_mechanisms.why_carried: Rejection depends on unproven downstream mint() behavior — unresolved execution-dependent question.

unresolved_mechanisms.source_evidence: onReceive/onRevert call mint(destinationAddress, zetaValue, internalSendHash) with no connector-side hash mapping.
unresolved_mechanisms.unresolved_question: Does mint() enforce internalSendHash uniqueness internally? Implementation not in source.

rejected_mechanisms.rejecting_source_fact: Solidity 0.8.7 has built-in overflow protection; addition reverts on overflow.
setMaxSupply() lets TSS set a meaningful value; default is configuration, not code defect; check logic structurally correct.
rejected_mechanisms.why_unexploitable: Operational configuration concern, not exploitable code defect.

impact_direction.attacker_receives: Phantom-ZetaSent tokens on destination chain (CEI path); double tokens if mint() lacks hash enforcement (replay path).
impact_direction.attacker_preserves: Pause-bypass: TSS preserves ability to mint frozen tokens.
impact_direction.victim_loses: Pause guarantee; cross-chain accounting integrity; all holders if supply inflated.
impact_direction.invariant_violated: (1) Pause: onReceive mints when paused. (2) CEI: mint before callback enables phantom flows. (3) Replay: no on-chain dedup of internalSendHash.
impact_direction.not_self_funded_or_dust_or_admin_or_timi: Pause-bypass affects emergency response; CEI path impact material; replay path (if mint lacks enforcement) permissionless at TSS submission layer with real inflation.

stop_condition: more_mechanisms_pending: pause invariant, CEI/callback accounting, replay dedup carried; mint() hash enforcement unresolved
